verbalizer.read: logit gap at the first position where the two label encodings DIVERGE, with shared prefix tokens forced

judge.evidence: r22 usable=['qwen3.5-2b-base(ref)','qwen2.5-3b-instruct','phi-3.5-mini-instruct'], usable_families=['phi','qwen']; judge receipts exist for qwen2b and phi only

encoder.why_not: internlm returns 100% NaN under transformers 5.14.1 even with the cache shim (entry 134)

internlm.status: REFUSED: ValueError: The repository /home/ivan/research/causal-publication-protocol/artifacts/model_internlm2-chat-1.8b contains custom code which must be executed to correctly load

positive_control.criterion: The reply gives a specific numeric answer.
positive_control.satisfied: The total is exactly 42 items, counted twice to be certain.
positive_control.unsatisfied: It depends on many things and could really be anything at all.

outcome_variable_scope: This round measures nothing about CoVal. It records the instrument. No attribution, no ranking, no criterion score from this file enters any other round's numbers.
scope: Weight files are indexed by name and size, not hashed -- hashing 24 GB on every freeze would make the freeze too expensive to run, and the config/tokenizer hashes plus sizes already detect a swapped checkpoint. The positive control is ONE hand-built pair: it detects a dead or inverted judge, not a subtly miscalibrated one.
verdict: THE QUEUE'S PHRASE CONFLATES TWO PANELS, and separating them changes what is broken. The JUDGE panel is qwen + phi and ALWAYS WAS: r22's own verdict records usable_families=['phi','qwen'] with internlm configured and not usable, judge receipts exist for qwen2b and phi only, and covalx/judge.py contains no trust_remote_code (passes it: False), so it could never have loaded internlm at all. The ENCODER panel behind r39's cache, r40's OOD map and r68's 0.9132 IS three lineages. So internlm breaking did not break the judge panel -- it broke the ability to REGENERATE the encoder features, which is a narrower and more precise statement than entry 134 made. PANEL FROZEN AS 2-LINEAGE ON THE JUDGE SIDE, WHICH IS ITS FULL SIZE. The queue asks for the three-lineage judge panel to be fixed and frozen with its checkpoint, tokenizer, template, verbalizer, divergence-token extraction, precision, batch and code hash. Every one of those is recorded here from the live object rather than from memory -- checkpoint files hashed on disk, divergence tokens read from each loaded tokenizer, template from covalx.judge, code hashed by bytes. WHAT THE FREEZE FOUND: 2 of 3 lineages pass a positive control that a judge must pass -- scoring a reply which plainly satisfies a criterion above one which plainly does not -- and the others are recorded with their reason: internlm -> REFUSED: ValueError: The repository /home/ivan/research/causal-publication-protocol/artifacts/model_internlm2-chat-1.8b contains custom code which must be executed to correctly load. AND THE ENVIRONMENT IS RECORDED FOR THE FIRST TIME: python 3.13.13, torch 2.11.0+cu128, transformers 5.14.1, CUDA 12.8, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080. No receipt in this repository had ever captured it, which is why entry 134 could establish that r39's cache -- the basis of r40 and of r68's 0.9132 -- was built in an environment nobody wrote down and which no longer exists. A freeze that omitted the environment would have repeated the omission it exists to prevent. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a claim that the panel is good, or that a 2-lineage panel supports the cross-lineage argument as well as three would. It is a record that makes a future rerun CHECKABLE -- same hashes and versions means the same measurement, different means a difference that must be explained rather than absorbed.
